items.followUp: Define ionization energy and give one example.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the electron addition to an isolated gaseous atom and the resulting negative ion.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity as the energy change when an electron is added to a gaseous atom to form a negative ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the process and the resulting negative ion; accept either energy released or energy change depending on convention used in the textbook wording.

rubric.why: A correct example shows an atom accepting an electron to form an anion.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as chlorine accepting an electron to form a chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid atom-to-negative-ion example.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom to form a negative ion.
For example, a chlorine atom gains an electron to form a chloride ion: Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻.

items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond is characterised by the sharing of three electron pairs.
rubric.description: States that three pairs (six electrons) are shared between the bonded atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the three shared pairs or six shared electrons.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates a triple covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as the nitrogen molecule, N₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A triple covalent bond is formed when two atoms share three pairs of electrons.
For example, the two nitrogen atoms in N₂ share three pairs of electrons.

items.followUp: Explain how a metallic bond holds metal atoms together.

rubric.why: Metal atoms form positive ions or kernels in the metallic structure.
rubric.description: Identifies the positively charged metal ions or kernels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the positive metal ions, cations or kernels.

rubric.why: The bond is the electrostatic attraction between the positive metal particles and delocalised electrons.
rubric.description: Describes the attraction between positive metal ions and the surrounding delocalised electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this electrostatic attraction.

modelAnswer: A metallic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between positively charged metal ions (kernels) and the sea of delocalised electrons around them.

items.followUp: State how electrons are shared in a polar covalent bond and in a non-polar covalent bond.

rubric.why: Unequal sharing of the bonding electrons produces a polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that electrons are shared unequally in a polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the unequal sharing distinction or its consequence, partial charges.

rubric.why: Equal sharing of bonding electrons distinguishes a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that electrons are shared equally in a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equal sharing distinction or its consequence.

modelAnswer: In a polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are attracted unequally by the two atoms.
In a non-polar covalent bond, the shared electrons are shared equally between the atoms.

items.followUp: Define mass/volume percentage concentration and write its formula.

rubric.why: Volume/volume percentage compares the volume of solute with the total volume of solution.
rubric.description: Identifies the ratio of the volume of solute to the volume of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct quantities in the ratio.

rubric.why: Multiplication by 100 expresses the ratio as a percentage.
rubric.description: States that the ratio is multiplied by 100, or gives the correct formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the factor 100 or writing the percentage formula.

modelAnswer: Volume/volume percentage is the volume of solute present in 100 volumes of solution.
Volume/volume % = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.

rubric.why: A concentrated solution contains a comparatively large quantity of solute.
rubric.description: States that the solution contains a relatively large amount of solute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the amount or concentration of solute as large or high.

rubric.why: The amount of solute is understood relative to a specified amount of solvent or solution.
rubric.description: Relates the solute amount to a given amount of solvent or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the reference amount of solvent or solution.

modelAnswer: A concentrated solution contains a relatively large amount of solute dissolved in a given amount of solvent.

items.followUp: Explain how electronegativity changes down a group in the periodic table.

rubric.why: Electropositivity increases as one moves down a group.
rubric.description: States the direction of the trend: electropositivity increases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend.

rubric.why: Increasing atomic size and decreasing attraction for outer electrons make electron loss easier down the group.
rubric.description: Gives a valid reason for the trend, such as increasing atomic size or easier loss of outer electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation.

modelAnswer: Electropositivity increases down a group in the periodic table.
Down the group, atomic size increases and the outer electrons are lost more easily.

items.followUp: Write down any two physical properties of copper.

rubric.description: Gives one correct property of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid property; do not award twice for synonyms of the same property.

rubric.why: A second distinct property completes the requested pair.
rubric.description: Gives a second correct property of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another valid property distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Silver is ductile and a good conductor of heat and electricity.
